Those “vessels of wrath” were not destroyed at once, but God bore with them long; and the “vessels of mercy” enter glory not because they deserve it, but because God had prepared this grace beforehand. This leaves us no choice but humility, because we are able to stand not because we are better.

Paul then explains plainly that God’s choosing is not limited by bloodline. It reaches not only the Jews but also the Gentiles. Those who were not a people have become a people; those who were not beloved are called beloved. This completely overturns people’s categories and boundaries. It is not background, performance, or qualification that determines identity, but God’s call and mercy that decide everything. This is the heart of the gospel: not people finding God, but God finding people.

Finally, the prophet’s message reminds us that even when the numbers are great, it is a “remnant” who are saved. This is not because God is stingy but because human hearts are often hard. If God had not taken the initiative to preserve mercy, our end would have been like Sodom and Gomorrah. Yet God still keeps a seed for himself so the flame of salvation is not extinguished. This helps us understand that being able to believe, repent, and follow Jesus today is itself a great grace and a miracle.
a: Put down comparison and give thanks
It is not that I am better than others, but that I have received more mercy.
Respond to God’s choosing with humility
Since it is grace, do not boast; simply obey and let Jesus be King.
See people with eyes of mercy
God could call me, and he can call anyone. Do not look down on others or judge them.
q: Do I sincerely admit that being a child of God today is entirely because of his mercy?
pr: Father, thank You for not treating me as I deserve but choosing me in mercy. When I am prone to self-righteousness, comparison, or judging, remind me that I am only a vessel that has received grace. Let me live humbly and obediently before You all my life, let Jesus be King in my life, and let me treat others with the same mercy. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I do not stand by my own strength; I live entirely in God’s mercy.

t: When You Feel Small, God Is Rejoicing Over You
v: From beyond the rivers of Cush, my worshipers, even the daughter of my dispersed people, will bring my offering.

In that day you will not be disappointed for all your doings in which you have transgressed against me; for then I will take away out from among you your proudly exulting ones, and you will no more be arrogant in my holy mountain.
But I will leave among you an afflicted and poor people, and they will take refuge in the LORD’s name.
The remnant of Israel will not do iniquity nor speak lies, neither will a deceitful tongue be found in their mouth, for they will feed and lie down, and no one will make them afraid.”
Sing, daughter of Zion! Shout, Israel! Be glad and rejoice with all your heart, daughter of Jerusalem.
The LORD has taken away your judgments. He has thrown out your enemy. The King of Israel, the LORD, is among you. You will not be afraid of evil any more.
In that day, it will be said to Jerusalem, “Don’t be afraid, Zion. Don’t let your hands be weak.”
The LORD, your God, is among you, a mighty one who will save. He will rejoice over you with joy. He will calm you in his love. He will rejoice over you with singing.
b: This passage shows us a profound reversal in the gospel. God does not choose the proud, the strong, and the boastful; he deliberately removes the arrogant and leaves only “an afflicted and poor people.” This is not because God likes people to suffer, but because only those who admit they are powerless, selfless, and in need of God can truly take refuge in the name of Yahweh. God’s Kingdom never belongs to the self-confident, but to those who are willing to let God be King.

The prophet then describes the remnant who are left: they no longer live in sin and deceit, nor in fear. “They will feed and lie down, and no one will make them afraid” does not mean the outward circumstances are perfect, but that the heart has found rest. It is a state of life surrounded by God’s presence. When people no longer grasp for security by themselves but trust in God alone, they enter true peace. This is a real picture of the 321 teaching of selflessness: letting Jesus live within.

Finally, the passage brings out a most startling scene: it is not people rejoicing over God, but God rejoicing over people. Yahweh is in your midst, rejoicing over you with joy, even “calming you in his love.” This is not because you perform so well, but because you belong to him. God’s love is not a noisy demand but a deep, steady, present love. When you are afraid, your hands are slack, and you feel small, God says: do not be afraid, I am in your midst, and I rejoice over you with singing.
a: Put down pride and admit you need God
Remind yourself every day: it is not I who can, but God who can.
Learn to take refuge in his name when anxious
When your heart is afraid, choose to trust instead of holding yourself up.
See yourself through God’s eyes
Even in my weakness, God still rejoices over me.
q: What pride or self-reliance do I most need to put down right now?
pr: Dear Father, thank You for not leaving me because of my weakness, but choosing to dwell in my midst when I am smallest and most in need of You. Take away the pride and fear in my heart, and teach me to trust You selflessly, letting Jesus be King in my life. When my hands are slack and I am afraid, strengthen me with Your presence. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: Yahweh is in my midst, and I am no longer afraid.

t: When You Doubt Who You Are, the Father Has Already Declared Your Identity
v: See how great a love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God! For this cause the world doesn’t know us, because it didn’t know him.
Beloved, now we are children of God. It is not yet revealed what we will be; but we know that when he is revealed, we will be like him, for we will see him just as he is.
Everyone who has this hope set on him purifies himself, even as he is pure.
b: John opens with “See,” as if asking us to stop and look again at a fact that is often overlooked yet utterly astonishing: we are called children of God, and not just in name but in true identity. None of this is because we are good enough or spiritual enough, but because of the “great love” the Father has given. This is the starting point of grace and the heart of the gospel. When people live in comparing their self-worth and in the world’s eyes, they easily get lost; but in the Father’s love, we are redefined.

John then reminds us of a spiritual tension: we are children of God “now,” but what we will be is “not yet revealed.” This is not uncertainty but hope. The future is not an unknown to fear but a sure glory, because we will be like the Lord Jesus and will see him as he is. This is not achieved by trying to imitate him but is the result of life being transformed. When people selflessly let Jesus be King, the Holy Spirit shapes Christ’s life in us step by step.

Finally, John connects hope to daily living. True hope does not make people relax; it brings a purified life. It is not suppressing sin by willpower, but because our eyes are fixed on Jesus that we naturally long to live in a way that pleases God. When we know we are God’s children, we no longer live for ourselves but willingly let our lives be guided by the Holy Spirit, becoming more and more like the Lord.
a: See yourself again through the Father’s love
Each day let God’s eyes, not the world’s labels, define you.
Fix your focus on future hope
Do not be trapped by present weakness; remember that you are being shaped to be like Jesus.
Live a pure life out of your identity
Not to perform, but because you belong to God.
q: Do I see myself now by the world’s standards, or by the Father’s love?
pr: Dear Father, thank You for accepting me with such great love and making me Your child. When I doubt and deny myself, strengthen me again with Your truth. Let me fix my eyes on Jesus, live in the hope of the future, and today be renewed by the Holy Spirit in my daily life, becoming more and more like the Lord. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, I pray. Amen.
dc: I am a beloved child of the Father, and my life is being shaped to be like Jesus.
